workflowArticle.primaryIntent: Decide which app-related files to retain while removing an unused Mac app, without equating leftover size with disposable data or immediately available disk space.
workflowArticle.title: Review app leftovers before removing an unused Mac app
workflowArticle.distinctAngle: The reviewability cost boundary: Nix Free gives totals, while Pro exposes individual paths. Distinguish uninstalling an app from investigating data growth in an app still used.
workflowArticle.leadDirection: Choose an uninstaller when the app itself is no longer needed; investigate storage growth separately when you intend to keep the app. Nix documents the former workflow; Breathing Room is not verified as an equivalent uninstaller.
sections: Decide whether to remove the app or keep it
Nix's detailed file review is a Pro workflow
Review paths, retain uncertain support data and keep backups
Trash/history is not a permanent recovery or free-space guarantee
For an app you keep, investigate storage rather than equating all app data with leftovers
workflowArticle.visualPlacement: Official cleared Nix Examine UI immediately after lead; selected labeled Breathing Room Space preview later at the keep-and-investigate branch. Do not embed until competitor rights gate clears.
workflowArticle.interactionPass: Handoff a local, non-mutating decision checklist: keeping app? unsure about a path? backup available? need per-file review? Output retain/investigate or review with documented uninstaller, never deletion commands or fabricated recovered bytes.
workflowArticle.safety: No hands-on tutorial claimed; no destructive commands. Do not recommend disabling Gatekeeper, granting permissions automatically, or emptying Trash to validate savings.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs Nix: investigation or uninstallation?
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between dedicated Mac app/leftover removal and broader ongoing maintenance investigation.
structure: When Breathing Room, which we build, may fit instead
Pricing, permissions, privacy and preview caveats
Link to workflow article and official sources
nixAdvantages: Dedicated uninstaller with documented Trash/history and leftover-review workflow (C04,C07,C12).
Documented one-time Pro offer rather than a recurring subscription, subject to two-device limit and major-version update wording (C06).
Vendor advertises Developer ID signing/notarization; Breathing Room's preview explicitly does not (C09,C13).
nixTradeoffs: Per-file details need Pro; 2 GB Free removal is lifetime cumulative (C04,C05).
Licence limits and diagnostic traffic qualify all-Macs/on-device headline wording (C06,C10,C11).
Requires macOS 14+ and documented Full Disk Access for leftover discovery (C02,C08).
breathingRoomAdvantages: Broader source-implemented storage/project exploration, grouped process monitoring and local activity history suit investigating apps still in use (C14).
Free local core and optional hosted AI Care rather than a paid app purchase (C13,C15).
breathingRoomTradeoffs: Preview limitations, Python 3.10+, lack of Developer ID/notarization and untested physical Intel behavior must be visible (C13).
Hosted AI requires authentication/network and can send relevant system information; paid recurring-care offer differs from a local-only utility (C15,C16).
No full app-uninstaller equivalence established; cannot promise Nix replacement (fit boundary).
